title: Frobenius compatibility of the canonical additive/coherent cohomology comparisons
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p$ [def-pc-field-characteristic], and let $X$ be a proper $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Put $G_X=(\mathcal O_X)_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module], and let $\mathrm{Fr}_X:G_X\to G_X$ be the additive sheaf map $s\mapsto s^p$. For $q\geq0$, put $E_X^q=H^q(X,\mathcal O_X)$ [pqf-def-cohomology]; let $F_X^q$ be Frobenius on the cohomology of the underlying Zariski abelian sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$, transported to $E_X^q$ by the canonical module/abelian cohomology identification [lem-sc-module-abelian-zariski-cohomology, def-sc-zariski-cohomology]. Let $c_X^q:H^q(X_{\mathrm{et}},G_X)\xrightarrow{\sim}E_X^q$ be the inverse of the canonical module-to-etale comparison [lem-sc-etale-zariski-qcoh-comparison]; equivalently it is the canonical etale-to-Zariski abelian comparison followed by the abelian-to-module identification just specified. Then $F_X^q$ is additive, $F_X^q(av)=a^pF_X^q(v)$, and
$$c_X^q\circ H^q(\mathrm{Fr}_X)=F_X^q\circ c_X^q.$$
For every field extension $k\subseteq K$ [def-pc-field-extension], put $X_K=X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-pc-base-change], let $j:X_K\to X$ be the projection and $u:j^{-1}G_X\to G_{X_K}$ the sheaf map whose adjoint is structural pullback of regular functions [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. With $P_j^q=H^q(u)\circ j^*$ the canonical additive-coefficient cohomology pullback [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback], let $b_q:E_X^q\otimes_kK\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{X_K}^q$ be the canonical flat coherent base-change isomorphism [lem-sc-flat-base-change-coherent]. Then
$$c_{X_K}^q(P_j^q(x))=b_q(c_X^q(x)\otimes1),\qquad F_{X_K}^q(b_q(v\otimes a))=b_q(F_X^q(v)\otimes a^p)$$
for every $x\in H^q(X_{\mathrm{et}},G_X)$, $v\in E_X^q$ and $a\in K$.

proof.text: Properness gives separatedness and finite type. The finite-type definition supplies a finite affine open cover $\mathcal U$ of $X$ over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Repeated application of the separated-affine-intersection lemma makes every positive-length tuple intersection affine, including repetitions. The inverse images of the opens cover $X_K$, and inverse image commutes with intersections. Apply the affine-triple tensor base-change theorem with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $X_0=Y_0=X$, $f_0=\mathrm{id}_X$, $W_0=S$, $U_0=V_0=U_J=\operatorname{Spec}A_J$, $B=C=A_J$, $\phi=\mathrm{id}_{A_J}$, and $T=\operatorname{Spec}K$: it identifies $j^{-1}U_J$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(K\otimes_k A_J)$, hence makes every target tuple affine. The structure sheaf is locally the module associated to the section ring itself, so it is quasi-coherent. Affine module vanishing applies on both schemes. For each affine intersection $U_J$, restriction of an ambient module injective resolution to $U_J$ is an injective resolution, by the module open-restriction lemma. Thus ambient derived evaluation at $U_J$ equals module cohomology of the scheme $U_J$. Apply the module/abelian comparison on that scheme. By the Zariski open-restriction lemma, restriction of an ambient abelian injective resolution is also an injective resolution, with exactly the same section complex at $U_J$. Consequently the resulting abelian vanishing on the scheme $U_J$ is precisely ambient abelian object-cohomology vanishing; apply the etale object-vanishing theorem with the unit quasi-coherent module to obtain etale vanishing. Thus the acyclic-edge hypotheses of Step 2 hold for all three cohomology theories on both schemes.

proof.text: Use the common section complex $C^r=\prod_J\mathcal O_X(U_J)$ with alternating restriction differential, and denote its canonical edges by $e_{et},e_{ab},e_{mod}$. The Zariski-to-etale inclusion is continuous, preserves the final object and tuple fibre products, and defines the change-of-site morphism by the cited inclusion theorem. For the associated unit module its restriction has exactly the Zariski sections and restrictions, by the definition of the associated etale sheaf: for $v:V\to X$, its unit pullback $v^*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_V\otimes_{v^{-1}\mathcal O_X}v^{-1}\mathcal O_X$ identifies with $\mathcal O_V$ via $r\otimes s\mapsto r\,v^\sharp(s)$, with inverse $r\mapsto r\otimes1$. Apply the general change-of-site edge square with identity coefficient map on these sections, and then its module-forgetting square. This gives $H^q(\epsilon)e_{ab}=e_{et}$ and $\iota e_{mod}=e_{ab}$, where $\iota$ is the canonical module-to-abelian identification. Consequently the canonical composite $H^q(\epsilon)\iota$ sends $e_{mod}[z]$ to $e_{et}[z]$, and its inverse sends $e_{et}[z]$ to $e_{mod}[z]$. This is $c_X^q$ by the specified etale-to-Zariski characterization in the statement; we do not infer canonicity from the existence-only statement of the quasi-coherent comparison theorem. All edges are isomorphisms by Step 1 and the acyclic-edge lemma. Apply these same two squares on $X_K$ with its base-changed cover to obtain $c_{X_K}^q e_{et,K}=e_{mod,K}$.

proof.text: On each section ring, $p\cdot1=0$ by its structural $k$-algebra map (also for the zero ring), so the binomial coefficients $\binom pi$ vanish for $0<i<p$, so $(s+t)^p=s^p+t^p$ and $(-s)^p=-s^p$ (also for $p=2$). Restrictions are ring maps, so the componentwise map $T(s_J)=(s_J^p)$ is additive and commutes with the alternating differential. Thus it acts on cycles modulo boundaries. Since $T(a z)=a^pT(z)$, its map on Cech cohomology is $p$-semilinear. Natural additive edge maps for the coefficient Frobenius identify $e_{et}[Tz]=H^q(\mathrm{Fr}_X)e_{et}[z]$ and $e_{ab}[Tz]=H^q(\mathrm{Fr}_{X,Zar})e_{ab}[z]$. Step 2 then identifies the transported Zariski Frobenius with $e_{mod}[z]\mapsto e_{mod}[Tz]$. Apply module-edge naturality to the $\mathcal O_X$-linear endomorphism given by multiplication by $a\in k$: its section and cohomology actions are scalar multiplication, so the module edge is $k$-linear, so this proves additivity, $F_X^q(av)=a^pF_X^q(v)$, and $c_X^qH^q(\mathrm{Fr}_X)=F_X^qc_X^q$. No module-linearity of Frobenius has been assumed.

proof.text: The etale base-change functor $W\mapsto W\times_X X_K$ preserves final objects and fibre products by the finite-limit theorem, and carries covers to covers by the continuity theorem. The algebraic-structures theorem supplies the set-theoretic inverse image, its finite-limit preservation and its adjunction to direct image. A left adjoint preserves colimits, so this defines a morphism of sites; the same theorem identifies its abelian inverse image and unit with the specified ones. On each tuple, the adjoint of $u$ is the structural ring map $j_J^\#: \mathcal O_X(U_J)\to\mathcal O_{X_K}(j^{-1}U_J)$. The general change-of-site edge square therefore computes precisely the unit-and-coefficient pullback of the cohomology-pullback definition: $P_j^q(e_{et}[z])=e_{et,K}[(j_J^\#z_J)_J]$. This uses the adjoint additive coefficient map, without identifying $j^{-1}G_X$ with $G_{X_K}$.

proof.text: A field extension is flat: choose a $k$-basis of $K$, so tensoring with $K$ is a direct sum of copies of the identity on vector spaces and is exact. On Zariski sites the inverse-image-of-opens functor takes $U_J$ to $j^{-1}U_J$, preserving the final object, coverings and intersections. Apply the general change-of-site edge square to the underlying abelian structural map $\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_{X_K}$, and use the module-forgetting square on each scheme. It gives $j_{coh}^q(e_{mod}[z])=e_{mod,K}[(j_J^\#z_J)_J]$ for the canonical additive coherent pullback. To identify the Ext presentation used by the flat-comparison definition with these derived module groups, use the explicitly constructed moduleCohomologyExtResolutionEquiv, not an unspecified natural equivalence. Its coefficient naturality and its direct-image edge formula identify the map for the structural module morphism $\varphi:\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_{X_K}$: first apply $H^q(\varphi)$ on $X$, then the identity-coefficient direct-image edge. In the Ext presentation this is exactly inverse image with the constant-integer-sheaf comparison followed by the coefficient map, as specified in the flat-comparison definition. The definition of module cohomology fmap uses the same resolution diagram for that composite; the canonical module/abelian identification is obtained by forgetting this resolution and comparing its acyclic section complex. Thus the additive map $j_{coh}^q$ above is the map extended by the specific flat comparison, so $b_q(v\otimes a)=a\,j_{coh}^q(v)$ (its tensor order is exchanged from $K\otimes_k E_X^q$). Apply module-edge naturality on $X_K$ to multiplication by $a\in K$, which is $\mathcal O_{X_K}$-linear. Thus $e_{mod,K}$ is $K$-linear, hence $b_q(e_{mod}[z]\otimes a)=e_{mod,K}[(a\,j_J^\#z_J)_J]$. The specific flat separated-cohomology theorem supplies invertibility of this very map: $X$ is compact (quasi-compact) by finite type, its structure morphism is separated, and the unit module is quasi-coherent. Taking $a=1$, Step 4 and the two canonical edge identities in Step 2 give $c_{X_K}^q(P_j^q(x))=b_q(c_X^q(x)\otimes1)$ for every $x$.

proof.text: For every tuple $J$, the ring-map property and commutativity give $(j_J^\#(z_J)a)^p=j_J^\#(z_J^p)a^p$. Therefore, if $v=e_{mod}[z]$, Step 3 on $X_K$ and Step 5 imply $F_{X_K}^q(b_q(v\otimes a))=e_{mod,K}[(j_J^\#(z_J^p)a^p)_J]=b_q(F_X^q(v)\otimes a^p)$. Every cohomology class has a Cech cycle representative by Step 1, so the identity holds for every $v$ and $a$. The tensor relation is respected: replacing $(\lambda v)\otimes a$ by $v\otimes\lambda a$ gives $F_X(v)\otimes\lambda^pa^p$ on both sides. Thus the formula does not require $k$ or $K$ to be perfect.
